title: Force UTF-8 CLI output so piped stdout is decodable on Windows
intent: Make the code_audit CLI write UTF-8 on stdout/stderr regardless of the host locale codepage, so piped or redirected output is decodable by a UTF-8 reader. This fixes the pre-existing Windows failure of the CLI/API parity tests, whose subprocess reads the child's pipe as UTF-8.

scope.out_of_scope_notes: Message content is unchanged; no non-ASCII characters were added, removed, or banned. File-write encoding is deliberately NOT addressed here and is recorded as follow-up CP1252-FILEWRITES-002: four text-mode open() calls in src/ lack an explicit encoding -- three reads (analyzers/deployment.py:108 YAML config, analyzers/routers.py:447 JSON analytics, analyzers/sql_ecosystem.py:87 YAML config) and one write (analyzers/routers.py:499 router_analysis.json) -- plus one Path.write_text() in tests/test_sql_ecosystem_analyzer.py:744. Same root cause (implicit locale encoding on Windows), different stream. The three reads are the more dangerous half: a UTF-8 config read as cp1252 either raises or silently mojibakes. PYTHONIOENCODING is deliberately NOT set in the parity test harness -- see why_not_redundant.

what_changed: Added a guarded sys.stdout/sys.stderr reconfigure(encoding='utf-8') at the top of main() in src/code_audit/__main__.py, before any output is produced, wrapped in try/except so a already-wrapped or redirected stream cannot break the entry point
Covered stderr as well as stdout, because the reproduction showed the undecodable cp1252 byte on both streams
diff_articulation.why_not_redundant: The observed failure is a decode error in the PARENT process, not an encode crash in the child: the child exits 2 normally and writes its em-dash as cp1252 byte 0x97, then subprocess.run's UTF-8 reader thread raises UnicodeDecodeError, dies, and leaves proc.stdout as None -- producing the json.loads(None) TypeError. Setting PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8 in the test harness also turns the test green, but it was rejected: it would make the parity test pass even if this production fix were later removed, destroying the only regression witness for it. Fixing the child's write encoding at the entry point fixes the parity tests and the real redirect path (code-audit <path> --json > out.json on Windows) with the same change.

commands_run: PYTHONPATH=<worktree>/src py -3.11 -m pytest tests/test_api_cli_parity_ci.py tests/test_cli_api_parity_debt_ci.py tests/test_cli_api_parity_scan_ci.py -q
test_results: Pre-fix reproduction: test_api_cli_parity_ci_default_scan_sample_repo_exceptions FAILED with TypeError: the JSON object must be str, bytes or bytearray, not NoneType, and UnicodeDecodeError: 'utf-8' codec can't decode byte 0x97 raised inside subprocess.py _readerthread
Post-fix targeted: 9 passed across the three CLI/API parity test files, with no PYTHONIOENCODING set
Post-fix full suite: 1223 tests collected across 123 files, 0 failed, 9 skipped, run reached 100% (addopts carries --maxfail=1, so completion is itself evidence of zero failures)
verification.notes: All runs pin PYTHONPATH to this worktree's src. Without that pin, 'python -m code_audit' on this machine resolves to C:/Users/thepr/Downloads/code-analysis-tool-fresh, which is checked out on feat/gate-wrong-artifact-detector at an incomplete WIP commit with a dirty tree that includes a modified __main__.py; any unpinned reproduction would be testing that tree instead of main. The 9 skips are pre-existing and unchanged by this patch; one of them (tests/test_sql_ecosystem_analyzer.py:744) is a Windows skipif for the same root cause on the file-write stream and remains correctly skipped under this fix.
